en.title: Maximum Security Sum When You Must Jump Out of the Network
en.description:
You must choose a starting point and collect its security value, then repeatedly jump +k and collect the value where you land, stopping only when the next jump would go out of bounds. You cannot stop early or choose nothing, and values may be negative; find the total for the best starting point.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n k, followed by n security values; original bounds 1≤n≤1000000, 1≤k≤n, −1000≤security[i]≤1000.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 7; -5; -2. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Compute, from right to left, the total from each starting point until leaving the array: dp[i]=a[i]+dp[i+k], where terms past the end count as 0; the maximum dp is the answer.
